title: Flatness characterized by first Tor with ideal quotients
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C$ an $R$-module. Then $C$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] if and only if $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,R/I)=0$ for every ideal $I\subseteq R$, where Tor is the first homology of a projective resolution tensored with the second module [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M5 (lemma-characterize-flat, line 18650), equivalence of (1) and (4), proof lines 18664-18688

proof.text: Let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal. Apply the first-variable Tor exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable] to $0\to I\to R\to R/I\to0$, tensoring with $C$. Since $R$ is free of rank one, the resolution concentrated in degree zero gives $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R,C)=0$ by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. Exactness therefore identifies $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(R/I,C)$ with the kernel of $I\otimes_RC\to R\otimes_RC=C$; the Tor symmetry [lem-weil-pbc-tor-symmetry] identifies this Tor group with $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,R/I)$. This is the kernel identity of Remark 00M6, with the maps specified by the exact sequence.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00M5 and Remark Tag 00M6 (remark-Tor-ring-mod-ideal), lines 18670-18696; Tor exact sequence Tag 00M0 and symmetry Tag 00M3

proof.text: If $C$ is flat, the inclusion $I\hookrightarrow R$ stays injective after tensoring with $C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Under $R\otimes_RC=C$, the resulting map is $I\otimes_RC\to C$. Step 1 makes $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,R/I)=0$. This holds for every ideal, including $I=0$ and $I=R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00M5 (lemma-characterize-flat), first paragraph, lines 18664-18668, specialized to degree one

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(C,R/I)=0$ for every ideal $I$. Step 1 says that $I\otimes_RC\to C$ is injective for each $I$, in particular for every finitely generated ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion] to conclude that $C$ is flat. For $I=0$ the map is $0\to C$; for $I=R$ it is the canonical isomorphism $R\otimes_RC\to C$, so neither edge case imposes a spurious condition.
